adopted_scope: Keep alphanumeric Glyph typography separate from punctuation typography inside the same original Word. Use it for notice-heading evidence; no layout reordering or new financial-frame grouping rule.
general_rule: Classify the glyphs of each exact source Word using the existing Unicode alphanumeric predicate, and retain the font/size identities of its alphanumeric glyphs separately from all glyph identities. Keep all-glyph provenance complete. Preserve this evidence with the same source occurrence through canonical Word sorting.
completeness: Reconstruct the complete emitted raw Word from the same increasing, unique original Glyph indices.
For opaque Identity CIDs, require the existing owned AJ1 source proof before assigning a Unicode class. Private/unknown character classes remain explicitly unknown.
Content style pairs must have finite positive sizes and belong to that same Word all-glyph style set.
Unknown, malformed, contradictory or conflicting duplicate occurrence evidence cannot authorize a heading.
Symbol-only headings retain complete original typography instead of requiring alphanumeric title content.
fixture_literals: Page/Word IDs and the original eight-enclosure label exist only in tests and static oracle data. No title string or period-number match was added to production.
negative_controls: A body-font alphanumeric glyph in a mixed Word stays part of content typography; punctuation handling must not discard that font. CJK, Latin, digit and kana cases are covered.
metamorphic_controls: Both all-glyph and content-glyph source font channels are renamed consistently; actual font bijection and reversed emission controls now cover eight original PDFs, including the repaired page.
remaining_legacy: Older length/line-count/fixed-point rules remain in financial_enclosures and other layout consumers. Source font identity is not a universal proof of visual font equivalence, visible ink, issuer identity or complete reading order.
